title: markdownpoint/agent/1
description: MarkdownPoint’s agent contract: each method with the scope it is served in, the params it takes and the result it answers, the envelope a request and its response travel in, and the error a failure gives.

schema.description: The answer is a JSON Schema, the contract describing itself.

AgentNoParams.description: What a method that takes nothing takes: no params, or an empty record.

app.description: The app that answers: its version, as `mdpoint --version` and MCP's server info give it.

methods.description: What the app serves itself, with no presentation, and what it serves for one.

operations.description: Operation types `proposals.create` takes; `schema` serves each one's exact request contract.

interpolations.description: The named interpolations; a key may instead carry four cubic-bezier numbers [x1, y1, x2, y2] with x within 0–1.

AgentCapabilities.description: The app's contract, the same whichever presentation is open, or none.

envelopeBytes.description: An envelope travels as one line, one string, so it is at most the longest string, counted in bytes: an ASCII envelope's characters.

longestEdge.description: The longest edge a rendered slide or frame can have: the longest side any export writes.

proposalOperations.description: Operations one proposal carries: it is applied as one kernel batch.

heldProposals.description: Proposals waiting at once: each stays in memory until it is accepted or rejected.

rangeSamples.description: Samples one `slides.frames` or `slides.measure` request takes: each renders the slide, and a frame's PNG is held until the answer is sent.

traceSamples.description: Samples one `slides.trace` request reads: each samples the whole animation once, and a frame rate times a range could reach billions.

selector.description: One operation's name, exports.run or themes.edit; omitted, the complete proposal request.

detail.description: `fields` answers with an index of the request's fields in place of its schema.

AgentSchemaSelector.description: What `schema` serves: one operation's request branch, the export request, or the whole proposal contract.

AgentWindow.description: A document window, as `windows.list` gives it: the presentation it shows, or null, and whether it is focused.

root.description: Absolute folder of an existing presentation.
The canonical root the app now shows.

opened.description: False when a window already showed it and was focused instead.

root.description: Absolute folder to create; its parent must exist and the folder must not.

theme.description: A bundled theme's name or key; the default theme when omitted.
The bundled theme it started from, by its key and name.

root.description: Absolute folder of a presentation a window shows.
The root whose windows closed, once each had saved.

AgentImageEditor.description: The external image editor, which only the app's own chooser sets.

AgentImageStylesResult.description: The style library, as the Restyle popup lists it; set one's `definition` as a picture's `restyle`.

definition.description: A style definition as images.styles.list lists them.

id.description: A style id from images.styles.list: the style to duplicate, delete or preview, the one save writes over, or the one export writes alone.

path.description: Absolute path of a styles file.

destination.description: Absolute path of a new .json file outside any presentation folder.

AgentImageStylesEditRequest.description: The Choose style… dialog's commands on the saved styles, which belong to this machine as its themes do: save a definition (as a new style, or over `id`), duplicate, delete, generate a style's preview pair (spending on OpenAI, as the dialog's Generate preview does), import a styles file and export one style or all to a file.

AgentImageStylesEditResult.description: The styles after the change; `selectedId` is the one saved, duplicated, imported or previewed, and `files` the export's file.

stalled.description: Present while the presentation cannot take in its files, as after a hand edit the parser refuses: `revision` and `issues` still describe the presentation as last read, and this says why the files on disk are not it, with the parser's errors about them.

outline.description: Its sections and slides in order.

date.description: A chosen Gregorian calendar date, independent of the render clock.

properties.description: The presentation's own properties as updatePresentationProperties sets them; an absent one is its default.

layouts.description: Each layout's placeholders, by the object's id insertSlide's content is keyed by and its type as the layout file spells it.

AgentRevision.description: An opaque revision from presentations.get, slides.get or an accept, naming the presentation as you last saw it; the one value that guards a change.

location.description: Where the problem stands, when its line is known.

fileScope.description: A file's issue: the folder its `path` is in, the presentation's or its theme's, since each may hold a file of that path.

AgentIssue.description: A problem with the presentation as the contract gives it: its English, where it stands and what the app does about it.

IssueLocation.description: Where in a presentation's files an issue stands: the file's name, and its line, counted from 1, and column when known.

RenderFileScope.description: Browser-safe file identity used between scene resolution and filesystem join: the presentation's own files, its theme's, or the models the app built from words' letters into its own cache on this computer.

AgentTextOverflowIssue.description: A presentations.get warning about words that run past their frame, where they still show; about words something hides, the slide's edge, the end of their path or their table cell, which an export asks about; or that this could not be measured.

PresentationSection.description: A section of the presentation: the .md file's header, its id and the name its heading line gives it.

PresentationNavigationSlide.description: A slide's place; a composition stands in no section and follows the slides.

PresentationTransitionSetting.description: Omission inherits; None explicitly disables the presentation's transition, and still starts on a click or by itself, a cut that moves on as an automatic transition does.

interpolation.description: The interpolation a carry-over or a scroll moves with; ease-in-out when omitted.

match.description: What a carry-over matches in text, as Keynote's Magic Move does: whole objects, or the words or characters two texts share; objects when omitted.

direction.description: Which way a push, scroll, move in, reveal or wipe travels across the screen; right to left (`left`) when omitted.

color.description: The color a fade passes through: a theme role or a hex color; black when omitted.

start.description: When it starts: `automatically` after the slide's last build, as Keynote's Start Transition Automatically; on a click when omitted.

delay.description: For one that starts by itself, the seconds it waits after the slide's last build ends, as Keynote's Delay; none when omitted.

PresentationTransition.description: The outgoing transition: a crossfade; Carry over, moving each object both slides share; the next slide pushing this one off, moving in over it, or revealed as this one moves off, in a direction; Scroll, both slides one strip the view travels across, this one held where it was left and the next playing its first step with the move; a wipe across it; a zoom in to it; or a fade through a color.

PresentationDefaultTextStyleSource.description: A default text style as presentation.json spells it: `none`, for a new text box with no style, or its style under `text-style`, as an object's, and its color.

PresentationBackgroundSource.description: A background as the file spells it.

FillSource.description: A fill as the file spells it: `none`, one color, or a gradient whose stops name their colors.

ColorSource.description: A color as the file spells it: a theme color by name, as `accent`, or a hex color, as `"#2F7D4F"`.

position.description: Where the stop stands along the gradient, 0–1.
Where the stop stands along the gradient, 0–1.

GradientFillSource.description: A gradient as the file spells it: its type, and stops that name their colors.

GradientLine.description: A linear gradient's own line: centered at (`x`, `y`) in frame fractions, `length` frame diagonals long. It may reach past the frame, holds while an outline morphs, and turns about its center with the angle.

GradientCenter.description: Where a radial gradient centers: a point in the box it paints, in fractions of it across and down, 0 at its top left.

PairSource.description: A pair of numbers as the file spells it.

PresentationShadow.description: An object's shadow: a drop shadow, or none. An object without the property casts none; "none" is written only to take back a shadow it would otherwise inherit from its layout or its presentation.

blur.description: A radius in canvas units, as every blur is.

offset.description: Canvas units across and down from the object, in the object's own turn.

color.description: A color role or CSS hex.

PresentationDropShadow.description: A drop shadow, as Keynote's Style › Shadow sets one: how soft, how far each way and in what color it falls.

AgentSlideId.description: A slide's stable id, as presentations.get and slides.get list it.

stepId.description: The step to sample; null selects Start.

time.description: Seconds within the step, at least 0.

AgentSlidePosition.description: A position in a slide's motion: Start, or seconds within a step, clamped to its effective duration.

steps.description: Ordered authored animation data from the same document and revision as the scene, in the file's words.

playbackStepIds.description: Ordered steps that consume presenter advances. Dormant authored steps remain in steps for editing.

motion.description: The master's motion setting, resolved for every consumer.

at.description: Null is Base. A sampled location reports the actual clamped time; Start has null stepId and time zero.

objects.description: The slide's objects as authored, before any animation, whatever `at` names: groups and each object's parent included, with the ids an edit names, each as the .mdpoint file spells it; the values at `at` are each target's `animationParameters` value.

provenance.description: Which theme level owns each object. Master and layout objects are the theme's; only a placeholder takes setContent.

animationValueSchemas.description: Each parameter's value domain by object type, then by parameter, once for each type on the slide that has it: a type holds its own range where it differs, as a text's scale and a model's do. The ordinary dry-run retains contextual admission.

trimStops.description: For each drawing, where its points fall along each contour as fractions of the contour's length: the values a trim key takes to stop at a point.

slideId.description: The slide or composition it is pinned to. A thread outlives its slide: one whose slide is gone is on a deleted slide.

name.description: The name they wrote it under; absent when they had none, and the reader's app names them in its own language.

PresentationCommentPosition.description: Fractions of the slide's width and height, independent of its current size.

start.description: Plays without a click of its own: with the step before it, or after that step ends, as PowerPoint's With Previous and After Previous do. Its times then count from that start. On the first step it plays after the transition. Omitted, the step waits for a click.

duration.description: Minimum seconds for this section; admitted later events extend its endpoint.

repeat.description: Play the section this many times before it completes; omitted plays once.

unstaggered.description: Every copy of a staggered repeat plays this step with its source instead of after its delay, as a transition carries each object whole. Only derived steps set it; a file cannot.

unanchored.description: Objects that turn and scale about their centers while this step plays, their anchors set aside until its end, as a transition carries each object as Keynote's Magic Move does. Only derived steps set it; a file cannot.

unplaced.description: Objects auto layout places that stay where this step's keys put them while it plays, their X and Y or a line's free ends, as a transition carries each object to its place on the next slide. Layout still gives each its room, so the others stand as they would; at the step's end layout places them again. Only derived steps set it; a file cannot.

PresentationAnimationCurveSource.description: A curve as the file spells it: its keyframes, its loop's word and the keyframe that loop starts from, the first when it names none.

anyOf.description: A geometry parameter as the file names it: a line's ends are its start and end.

ConstraintStrengthParameter.description: A model's constraint's strength, by the constraint's id, as `constraints.<id>.strength`.

value.description: Null clears an optional property; its current type-style/default then applies.
Original interpolation endpoint, admitted against the same target as value.

end.description: Original endpoint in section seconds; must be at or after time and does not extend the section.

incoming.description: Preserve an interpolation prefix before this key; at time, value applies immediately.

exponential-scale.description: Whether the move to this key scales at an even rate, as After Effects' Exponential Scale does.

oscillate.description: A swing added from this key on, its wave named as the file names it.

id.description: Caller-minted stable ID; new keys/cues share one unique namespace within the step. Reusing an ID replaces the whole event.

start.description: When the move into this key begins, in section seconds; until then the value before it holds. Absent, at the key before.

time.description: Nonnegative seconds, kept to the microsecond.

interpolation.description: Interpolation into this key, from the preceding key or section start.

path.description: On a path pair's x key, `frame.x` or `translation.x`: the move into it, with the pair's y key there, bends along this path.

PresentationAnimationKeyframeSource.description: A key as the file spells it: a move's `end` and `exponential-scale`, and a fill as the object spells its fill.

anyOf.description: What a key holds: a number, a flag, a color or a role, a fill, lengths, a shadow, or a 3D object's whole orientation.

PresentationAnimationValueSource.description: A value as the file spells it: a fill as `accent` or a gradient whose stops name their colors.

PresentationOrientation.description: A 3D object's orientation in quaternion mode, whole, its w with x, y and z: a quaternion of length 1.

frequency.description: Cycles a second, as After Effects' wiggle() frequency sets it; a noise wanders at that rate.

phase.description: Degrees into the cycle at the key.

seed.description: Which noise a noise wave draws, as Motion's Random Seed picks one; the same seed always draws the same.

PresentationAnimationOscillationSource.description: A swing as the file spells it: its wave is `wave-shape`.

PresentationAnimationBezier.description: A cubic Bézier easing as CSS spells it: two control points with time on x within 0–1 and value on y, which may overshoot.

PresentationAnimationCurveEasing.description: A named curve with its settings, the key-interpolation record: Blender's Back with its back, its Elastic with an amplitude and a period, its Bounce with a bounciness, or a spring.

PresentationAnimationBackEasing.description: Blender's Back with its Back setting: how far anticipate winds up, overshoot swings past its key, or both.

PresentationAnimationElasticEasing.description: Blender's Elastic ringing into its key: its ring as a multiple of the move, and its length in seconds, or 0.3 of the move.

PresentationAnimationBounceEasing.description: Blender's Bounce at a bounciness, Blender's Rigid Body word for a rebound's share of the speed it lands with.

PresentationAnimationSpring.description: A spring landing on its key: `amount` sets how far it swings past, from 0, which settles with no overshoot, to 1, and `response` its period in seconds as SwiftUI's does, or it fits the key.

orient.description: Turn the object to face along the path as it moves.

PresentationAnimationPath.description: A path in chord space: the start is (0, 0), the end (1, 0), and one unit across is a chord length right of travel.

id.description: Caller-minted stable ID, unique together with keys in this step.

time.description: Nonnegative seconds, kept to the microsecond.

PresentationStepCueSource.description: What a cue starts, as the file spells it: its `type`, and a clip's `media-trim`, `blend-in` and `clip-scale`.

MediaTrim.description: The span of its file a movie or sound plays, in seconds. Its end, when given, is after its start. A loop repeats it.

PresentationMotion.description: The one in-slide motion setting: how long a step's fade or move takes, set on the master.

stepId.description: Null selects the explicit starting state before the first click.

waited.description: The seconds the presentation waited past each played click's end, by the click's id as `playedPresentationAnimation` names it, the current click's running wait among them: a clip plays on while the presenter waits. Absent, each click followed the last at once, as the timeline is authored.

running.description: A clock that runs on past its click's end, as a show waits: what loops in the click plays on. Without it, a location at or past its click's end shows the click as it completed, every step at its own end and no loop playing: what a still picture of the click's end shows and the next click starts from. Before its end a click plays either way.

anyOf.description: The letters' color, or a gradient spanning the text's box that paints them, as Keynote's Gradient Fill.

AgentSlideObject.description: An object as the .mdpoint file spells it, with its words when it holds text (a text box, a shape, a table, a chart): exactly the Markdown setContent takes, so writing it back unchanged changes nothing; "" for empty words. A paragraph's `<!-- id: … -->` at the end of its last line is the id a step's text cue names it by, and it travels with its paragraph: words written without it keep each paragraph's id where its words start, a split's first part keeps it, and a join keeps the first paragraph's. Give a new paragraph none, so the app gives it one and its own step. Words that leave out a paragraph a step's cue names are refused, naming the step: keep the paragraph's id, or remove the cue first.

PresentationTransformFrame.description: The frame a transform gives an object: every side, but a table's height only where the edit sizes the table, as a move leaves its rows as they are.

TextModelFileSource.description: A text's 3D model as the file spells it.

ResolvedModelPose.description: A model's pose: the Action its latest clip plays, with its trim and `loop` when the clip repeats, and how far it has played, as the Action's seconds since the cue, its Clip Scale applied, or, with a stride, as the cycles its travel covers. `modelActionTime` turns it into the Action's seconds with the facts of the Action a renderer loaded. It stands over the pose `under` it, the clip before it, or over the rest pose without one, whole or, while it blends in, at its `influence`; a channel its Action doesn't key stays as it is under it.

PresentationTextFit.description: How a text frame follows its words: it grows to them on both sides, on one, or keeps the size it was given.

from.description: The pose each unit arrives from; a unit leaving by the same entrance returns to it.

spread.description: Units in flight at once, at least 1.

based-on.description: What arrives in turn, as After Effects' Range Selector bases it on; the file's `based-on`.

delivery.description: By paragraph: each paragraph arrives on a step of its own, the one its cue stands in, taking `duration` seconds, as Keynote's Delivery and PowerPoint's By Paragraph deliver a build. Absent, every piece arrives as `progress` says.

duration.description: With delivery alone: how long each paragraph takes to arrive, in seconds.

interpolation.description: How each unit travels from its pose to its place, on its own; linear when absent.

spaces.description: By character: each space is a unit too, keeping its turn.

fade.description: Opacity's own share of each unit's travel, on the travel's interpolation.

order.description: Which unit arrives first; absent, the first unit.

seed.description: Which shuffle a random order takes; absent, the first.

pause.description: How long the entrance holds wherever the next unit to arrive lies in another paragraph, in units' time; absent, none.

TextEnterSource.description: A text's entrance, its pose, spread and progress left out where they are the defaults, as the file writes it.

blur.description: Em of blur, a radius as every blur is.

PresentationTextPose.description: Where an arriving unit starts, as Motion's Sequence Text: absent values are its place; offsets and blur are in its font size.

to.description: The pose each unit exits to, as Motion's Sequence Text sequences To: absent values are its place.

spread.description: Units in flight at once, at least 1.

based-on.description: What arrives in turn, as After Effects' Range Selector bases it on; the file's `based-on`.

interpolation.description: How each unit travels from its pose to its place, on its own; linear when absent.

spaces.description: By character: each space is a unit too, keeping its turn.

fade.description: Opacity's own share of each unit's travel, on the travel's interpolation.

order.description: Which unit arrives first; absent, the first unit.

seed.description: Which shuffle a random order takes; absent, the first.

pause.description: How long the entrance holds wherever the next unit to arrive lies in another paragraph, in units' time; absent, none.

TextExitSource.description: A text's exit, written as its entrance is.

PresentationRowEnter.description: Sampled only: a paragraph its cue brings in, under an entrance delivered by paragraph, `progress` of the way from the entrance's pose to its place, 0 to 1, on its curve and with its fade.

PresentationCounterWheel.description: One digit of a rolling counter: where its wheel stands, 0–10 with 10 the 0 after 9, and how visible it is.

PresentationAnchor.description: Where an object's animated turn and scale pivot, as fractions across and down its frame: 0 to 1 within it, and past it beside it.

PresentationScale2d.description: A single object's scale along its own x and y axes.

angle.description: Degrees clockwise from up of the direction the edge travels, as After Effects' Wipe Angle.

feather.description: The soft edge's width in canvas units.

PresentationWipe.description: A linear wipe, as After Effects': a feathered edge travels at its angle; progress 0 hides, 1 shows all.

CompositionBindings.description: Property name to input name; `text` and `file` name the object's content.

PresentationTextDirection.description: The side a text box's lines start on: the left, or the right for words written right to left, as Arabic and Hebrew are.

PresentationObjectLevel.description: Where a materialized object came from and which of its properties the slide overrides.

value.description: Effective value in authored parameter space before ancestor group poses; omitted when no value or default exists.

longestEdge.description: Maximum PNG edge in pixels, preserving the slide's aspect ratio. Defaults to 1024.

destination.description: Absolute path of a new .png file outside any presentation folder, which the app writes instead of returning the image inline; the result then names it in files and carries no image.

AgentLongestEdge.description: The longest edge of a rendered picture in pixels, the slide's aspect ratio kept, up to capabilities' limits.longestEdge.

AgentSlideView.description: slide (the default) as the audience sees it; top or left for the slide's 3D content from above, the audience at the bottom, or from the slide's left, the audience on the right, with the slide's plane and its shadow catchers' planes drawn in and lines from the slide's corners toward its camera, to judge depth a front view hides. A slide with no 3D content has no top or side view.

overflowing.description: Objects whose text does not fit their frames at this position, taller or wider than the box, as the canvas marks them.

fittedFrames.description: The frame each text object takes when fitted to its text at this position, in its own parameters there, to write with transformObjects at the same position: `height` as Fit box to text and the bottom handle fit it, the top kept; `width` as a side handle fits it, every paragraph on one line, the point its alignment holds kept. Its letters stay where they stand whatever its turn, scale and anchor. A box that grows to its words already stands at its `height`, the height its words take, which no file holds. Text in columns has no `width`; objects with no text are left out.

textBounds.description: Where each object's words stand at this position, in canvas units, as After Effects' sourceRectAtTime reads a text layer's: the axis-aligned union of its lines' boxes, its pose included. Objects with no words are left out.

overflowing.description: Objects whose text does not fit their frames at this position, taller or wider than the box, as the canvas marks them.

fittedFrames.description: The frame each text object takes when fitted to its text at this position, in its own parameters there, to write with transformObjects at the same position: `height` as Fit box to text and the bottom handle fit it, the top kept; `width` as a side handle fits it, every paragraph on one line, the point its alignment holds kept. Its letters stay where they stand whatever its turn, scale and anchor. A box that grows to its words already stands at its `height`, the height its words take, which no file holds. Text in columns has no `width`; objects with no text are left out.

textBounds.description: Where each object's words stand at this position, in canvas units, as After Effects' sourceRectAtTime reads a text layer's: the axis-aligned union of its lines' boxes, its pose included. Objects with no words are left out.

AgentSlideRenderResult.description: The PNG in the answer, or with a destination the one file written, in `files`.

AgentFrame.description: A box on the slide in canvas units, as the kernel's own frame: an object's, its words' or a model's bounds.

from.description: Seconds within the step where the range starts. Defaults to 0.

to.description: Seconds within the step where the range ends, inclusive. Defaults to the end of the step's last pass.

stepId.description: The step whose time the frames sample, from slides.get; omitted with `transition`.

transition.description: Render the slide's transition into the next shown slide instead of a step, from 0 to its duration in seconds; omit stepId.

longestEdge.description: Maximum frame edge in pixels, preserving the slide's aspect ratio. Defaults to 512.

destination.description: A new or empty folder outside any presentation folder, which the frames are written into as frame-0001.png onward beside sheet.png; the result names them in files. Omitted, only the sheet returns.

AgentStepSeconds.description: Seconds within a step, as the step's own times read them.

times.description: Each frame's time within the step or the transition, in order.

sheet.description: Every frame in a grid, left to right and top to bottom, each labeled with its time.

files.description: With a destination, the frames written in order and then the sheet.

stepId.description: The step whose time is sampled, from slides.get.

from.description: Seconds within the step where the range starts. Defaults to 0.

to.description: Seconds within the step where the range ends, inclusive. Defaults to the end of the step's last pass.

AgentStepRange.description: A span of one step's time, sampled at a rate: `from` 0 and `to` the end of its last pass when omitted, 30 per second.

channels.description: Each parameter the step keys, sampled at every time in authored parameter space, before ancestor group poses.

AgentSlideMeasureRequest.description: What `slides.measure` takes: a step's range, or the slide's rests.

stepId.description: The step whose time is sampled, from slides.get.

from.description: Seconds within the step where the range starts. Defaults to 0.

to.description: Seconds within the step where the range ends, inclusive. Defaults to the end of the step's last pass.

fps.description: Samples per second over a step. Defaults to 10.

AgentStepMeasureRequest.description: A step's range as `slides.measure` samples it, 10 times a second by default.

rests.description: Measure the slide at every rest its show makes instead of a step; omit stepId, from and to.

fps.description: Samples per second over a rest that loops. Defaults to 30.

AgentSlideRestsRequest.description: A slide measured at each rest its show makes, in place of a step's range: over a rest that loops, `fps` samples a second, 30 when omitted.

floorGap.description: How far its lowest point stands above the slide's floor, its highest floor object, in canvas units.

AgentModelMeasure.description: A model at one time: its bounds and its shadows' on the slide, what it covers of each text, and its gap to the floor.

AgentTextCover.description: How much of a text's box a model's bounds overlap, how much of the text the model covers, and how much of its box the model's shadow does, 0 to 1. A model covers flat words where its silhouette lies over their box, in front or behind, and 3D words, which their own model draws, where it draws in front of their letters.

AgentFootSlip.description: How fast a walking model's planted foot slides across the floor against how fast its body travels, canvas units a second. The foot is a joint of the model's file, `node` its glTF node index, which tells two feet named alike apart, and `foot` its name as the file spells it, or "(node N)" for an unnamed one.

AgentWalkSpeed.description: The speed an in-place walk travels at this model's size, canvas units a second, at which its planted feet hold.

AgentTextSummary.description: The most any model covers a text and its shadow does, when and which, and the spans of time either is on it.

after.description: `entry` for the rest as the slide has appeared, or the step that leads the click it follows.

before.description: The step that leads the click that ends it; null after the last.

slideAge.description: Seconds since the slide began to appear, as it settles.

tail.description: `still` holds; `loop` repeats every `period` seconds; `live` moves on in no cycle a show repeats, measured as its last motion that ends does.

samples.description: Each moment measured, `time` seconds into the rest: how much of each object draws, 0 to 1, its opacity and its groups', 0 while hidden; and each model and 3D text's measures, as `slides_measure` gives them for a step.

AgentSlideRest.description: Where a show holds the slide until the next click, or after its last: once the click's steps, their "with" and "after" members, its Actions and the camera's drift have all ended. Measured as it settles, and over one period while it loops.

AgentRestTextSummary.description: The most any model covers a text at the slide's rests, as a sample's `covered` says, and its shadow does, and where: counted only while both draw.

objectId.description: A text object on that slide.

AgentSlideLettersRequest.description: One text object's letters, where its slide draws them at rest.

AgentObjectId.description: An object's id on its slide, as `slides.get` lists it.

letters.description: In reading order; spaces draw nothing and are left out.

text.description: The graphemes it draws: one, or several for a ligature.

pen.description: Its pen, on the baseline it stands on.

ink.description: The box of its ink, the font's own outline, upright on the slide; absent for a letter that draws nothing.

AgentLetter.description: A letter of a text where its slide draws it at rest, in canvas units: what a model sits on, lands on or points at.

AgentRequestId.description: A UUID the caller makes for its request, in either case.

fonts.description: The fonts the file carries, which PowerPoint shows wherever it opens.

missingFonts.description: The families the theme names that the file does not carry; their words are set in the fonts MarkdownPoint includes.

id.description: The id of the movie export to cancel, as its exports.run request gave it.

canceled.description: True means cancellation was requested for the matching active movie; its original awaited response reports the outcome.

objectId.description: A picture object on that slide.

path.description: Absolute path of the media file on this machine; or name and data in its place.

name.description: File name with the media's extension, such as photo.png, with data in place of path.

data.description: The file's bytes in base64, with name.

AgentMediaImportRequest.description: A picture, video or sound copied into the presentation's folder, as the media picker or a drop copies one: from a file on this machine by its absolute path, or from its bytes (base64) under a file name whose extension names its kind.

AgentMediaImportResult.description: The file's path in the presentation, as an object names it, and the object type it makes; `warnings` says what the import kept without, such as a movie's poster.

bounds.description: The exact box around every vertex at rest.

height.description: The rest height, and whether the model stands on y = 0 within a hundredth of it.

hiddenAtRest.description: Parts at rest scaled to nothing, as glTF has no visibility of its own: only the topmost of them.

castsNoShadow.description: Nodes whose extras.markdownpoint say they cast no shadow.

GlbVector.description: A model's GLB, read as three.js draws it: every vertex posed through its node transforms, morph weights and skin, so the bounds core measures are where the renderer puts the model. Core reads plain glTF 2.0 geometry from a GLB's own BIN chunk. Import has already decompressed Draco and meshopt and packed every file in, so data that would still need a decoder or another file is refused rather than read as nothing.

name.description: The Action's name, as `glbActionNames` gives it: the file's, or "Animation 1", "Animation 2" in file order for an unnamed one.

start.description: Its first key, in seconds on the file's clock. An Action's time 0 is the file's 0, so it may start late.

duration.description: Its last key: how long it plays from the file's 0.

loop.description: The Action's own `loop` in its extras.markdownpoint, or null when it says neither.

bounds.description: The box around every vertex over the whole Action.

lowest.description: Its lowest point and when, against a floor at y = 0.

seam.description: How far any vertex is between the Action's first frame and its last: what a loop jumps by.

weights.description: The range of the morph weights it plays, or null when it has none.

stride.description: For a model with feet, what its Action does with them.

GlbStride.description: How far a walk or run played in place carries the character per loop, in the model's units: "in place" when its planted feet slide back at one speed, "root motion" when the Action moves the character itself, "not a walk" otherwise.

GlbFoot.description: A foot of a walk: the joint by its glTF node index, which names it exactly, and its name as the file spells it, or "(node N)" for an unnamed one, for a reader; how much of the Action it stands planted, and how fast it slides then.

file.description: The model's path, such as media/bird-1a2b3c4d.glb.

AgentModelInspectRequest.description: A model of the presentation, by its file's path.

data.description: Any JSON the build reads, such as sizes or colors. With for and no source: { depth?, bevel? } in ems. The model's file keeps them.

for.description: A text object whose words the build makes 3D: data.words holds its letters, as its page lays them out at rest.

bounds.description: The exact box around every vertex at rest.

height.description: The rest height, and whether the model stands on y = 0 within a hundredth of it.

hiddenAtRest.description: Parts at rest scaled to nothing, as glTF has no visibility of its own: only the topmost of them.

castsNoShadow.description: Nodes whose extras.markdownpoint say they cast no shadow.

AgentModelInspectResult.description: What a model does. For letters the app built: the text they came from, and their depth and bevel.

name.description: The model's file name without extension, such as bird.

source.description: The build: an ES module with a default export build(kit, data). No file keeps it. Left out with for, the app's letter builder makes the words: kit.text(data.words, { depth, bevel }).

data.description: Any JSON the build reads, such as sizes or colors. With for and no source: { depth?, bevel? } in ems. The model's file keeps them.

models.description: The presentation's models the build loads with kit.model, by file path, such as a model models_animate gave actions.

for.description: A text object whose words the build makes 3D: data.words holds its letters, as its page lays them out at rest.

AgentModelBuildRequest.description: A model to build from source in the build window, saved as media/<name>-<hash>.glb, or a text's as generated/<name>-<hash>.glb.

violations.description: What the window's policy refused while the build ran.

built-from.description: With for: the built-from the text's model carries, { file, built-from }, to show while its words are these.

AgentModelBuildResult.description: The saved model, what import changed in the build's GLB, what the model does, and its sheet.

filter.description: Words the action's name or category must hold, such as walk inplace.

AgentModelActionsRequest.description: Meshy's actions whose name or category holds every word of `filter`.

prompt.description: What the picture shows, worded as the "Make models with Meshy" section of the MarkdownPoint skill says. Settings > Coding agents installs the skill.

character.description: A person or creature to rig: one figure in a T-pose.

AgentModelPictureRequest.description: A picture Meshy draws from `prompt`, the first step of a model; a character stands alone in a T-pose, ready to rig.

AgentModelPictureResult.description: Meshy's picture, which isn't saved in the presentation: `picture` names it to models_generate until `expires`, an ISO date-time as the file writes `created`; `credits` is what it cost.

name.description: The model's file name without extension, such as rocket.

file.description: A picture of the presentation instead, such as media/rocket-1a2b3c4d.png.

character.description: A figure to rig, in a T-pose.

AgentModelGenerateRequest.description: A model Meshy makes from a picture, saved as media/<name>-<hash>.glb: `picture` from models_picture, or `file`, a picture of the presentation. A character's comes in a T-pose, ready for models_rig.

AgentModelMeshyResult.description: A model Meshy made, saved: what cleaning and import changed, what it does, the credits it cost and its sheet.

file.description: The model to rig, such as media/figure-1a2b3c4d.glb.

name.description: The rigged model's file name; the model's with -rigged when left out.

AgentModelRigRequest.description: A model of the presentation for Meshy to rig, a humanoid facing +Z, `height` meters tall.

file.description: A model models_rig made, or one models_animate made from it.

actions.description: Action ids from models_actions, in the order the Actions should come.

loop.description: Names of the Actions to loop, as models_actions names them.

name.description: The animated model's file name; the model's when left out.

AgentModelAnimateRequest.description: Actions of Meshy's library, by id, on a model Meshy rigged; `loop` names the Actions to close on their cycle.

AgentMeshyActionId.description: An action of Meshy's library, by the whole-number id models_actions lists it by.

slideId.description: The slide the picture or background is on.

objectId.description: A picture object on that slide; omit for the slide's background.

restyle.description: true for the restyle of the picture or the slide's background, made from its image as first made, rather than its prompt.

AgentImageTarget.description: The image a generation is for, as the inspector's image sections name it: a picture by `objectId` on `slideId`, or the slide's background by `slideId` alone. `restyle` is the restyle of the picture or the background, generated from its current image as its Restyle section does, rather than from its prompt.

AgentImagePrepareResult.description: What generating would do, as the app's confirmation shows it: the provider and model it would use, whether it pays a provider (`requiresProvider`) or reuses an image already made for the same settings, and a `token` that `images.generate` spends. The prompt, transparency and style are the target's own properties, set as edits.

AgentImageVariant.description: A generated image kept for the target, as the variant strip shows them; `current` is the one in use.

token.description: The token images.prepare returned; it is spent once and expires.

AgentImageGenerateResult.description: `generatedUnselected`: the target changed while its image was made, so it is kept among the variants, unused.

slideId.description: The slide the picture or background is on.

objectId.description: A picture object on that slide; omit for the slide's background.

restyle.description: true for the restyle of the picture or the slide's background, made from its image as first made, rather than its prompt.

status.description: noChange when the image already shows the variant.

AgentMutationStatus.description: A mutation's own outcome: applied, or noChange when it left the presentation as it was. Its other facts stand beside it.

slideId.description: The slide whose words the prompt is drawn from.

current.description: The key of the theme the presentation uses; null when its master is in no listed theme.

key.description: The theme's key, its folder's name; `themes.use` and `themes.manage` take it or the name.

id.description: Its master's id, a lowercase UUID, as `presentations.get` gives the master in use; null while its master cannot be read.

width.description: The theme's slide size; null while its master cannot be read.

layouts.description: Its layouts, by the key the slides, `themes.manage` and `themes.edit` name them by.

AgentThemeSummary.description: One theme the presentation can change to: the themes its chooser lists.

theme.description: A theme's key or name from `themes.list`.

rescale.description: Required when the theme's slide size differs: fit keeps everything on the slide, fill covers it.

AgentThemeUseRequest.description: Change the presentation's theme, as the app's theme chooser does; slides keep their layouts by name.

status.description: noChange when the presentation already uses the theme.

theme.description: The theme the presentation uses now, by its key and name.

rescaled.description: The policy the slides were rescaled by; null when the sizes matched.

themeRevision.description: Guards `themes.edit`, and the theme step of `history.undo`/`history.redo`.

master.description: The master's settings as the file names them.

AgentThemeGetResult.description: The presentation's theme as Edit theme edits it: the master and each layout, authored values only.

step-duration.description: How long a slide step's fade or move takes; null takes the format's default.

schemes.description: `light`, `dark`, then every named scheme in file order.

objects.description: Its own objects, back to front, whose names a layout's placeholder can't take.

artwork.description: The master's own pictures by object id: one file, or one per scheme.

MasterEditableSource.description: The master as the file names its settings, for the Agent: its `layout-order` and `text-styles`, its guides and grid as the file writes them, and its `step-duration`.

properties.description: Property values as authored, spelled as text (`"1.05"`, `"text"`, `"upper"`).

MasterGuideSource.description: A guide as the file writes it: at `x` an upright line, at `y` a level one.

MasterGuidePlaceSource.description: A guide's place as the file writes it: canvas units, or a percentage such as "50%".

MasterGridSource.description: A grid as the file writes it: its columns, with a gutter and margin of 0 when left out, and its baseline from its start at its increment.

MasterAuthoredFont.description: The settings of a theme's documents as their editors change them: the master's fonts, colors, text styles, guides, grid, motion and layout order, a layout's name and scheme, which of its words and pictures are placeholders, and a theme picture's file per scheme. Each edit changes the document's authored values and is accepted only when the document it leaves reads back, so no edit writes a file the next read would refuse.

roles.description: Role values as authored: a CSS hex or `{brand.<name>}`.

ThemeFile.description: A theme's own picture: one theme-relative file, or one per scheme, `light` and `dark` among them.

name.description: The name the chooser shows: the file's, or one spelled from the key.

objects.description: Its own objects, back to front.

artwork.description: Its own pictures by object id: one file, or one per scheme.

LayoutEditableDocument.description: A layout as its pane and inspector show it.

LayoutEditableSlot.description: One placeholder of a layout: the slot a slide fills by its id.

AgentAnimationAim.description: Where in a slide's motion an edit lands, as the Animate tab's playhead aims the Inspector and the key buttons: at Start (`stepId` null), or at `time` in a step.

PresentationReplicaArrangement.description: A replica's copies in a grid a gap apart, or a ring a radius from the selection's center, as groups and repeats.

PresentationInsertObjectSource.description: An object to insert, in the file's words. A path is drawn either through `d` or through `points`.

anyOf.description: The letters' color, or a gradient spanning the text's box that paints them, as Keynote's Gradient Fill.

InsertText.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

InsertTable.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PresentationTableFrame.description: A table's frame as the files hold it: its height is its rows', and never stored.

InsertImage.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

end-opacity.description: The last copy's opacity, 0–1, the copies between fading evenly from the original's, as After Effects' Repeater's End Opacity.

position-randomness.description: How far, in canvas units, each copy may stand from its place, chosen by the seed.

rotation-randomness.description: How many degrees each copy may turn either way about its center, as Motion's Replicator's Angle Randomness.

scale-randomness.description: How far each copy's size may vary either way, as a fraction of it, as Motion's Replicator's Scale Randomness.

stagger-randomness.description: Up to how many seconds more each copy may wait before it plays, beyond its stagger.

seed.description: Which variation the copies take, as Motion's Random Seed: the same number gives the same copies everywhere.

ObjectFlip.description: An object mirrored in its frame: across its vertical axis, its horizontal one, or both.

InsertVideo.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

InsertAudio.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

anyOf.description: The letters' color, or a gradient spanning the text's box that paints them, as Keynote's Gradient Fill.

InsertShape.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

InsertIcon.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

InsertLine.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

at.description: Last checkpoint or deletion position; a live target takes precedence.

start.description: Fraction of each contour's length where the visible stroke begins.

end.description: Fraction of each contour's length where the visible stroke ends.

InsertGroup.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

AutoLayoutSource.description: An auto layout as the file spells it, its reference point `reference-point`, left out at start.

InsertComposition.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

anyOf.description: The letters' color, or a gradient spanning the text's box that paints them, as Keynote's Gradient Fill.

InsertChart.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PresentationChartType.description: What a chart draws from its table: columns standing up from or bars lying along its categories, side by side or stacked, a line or a stacked area per series, a pie or a donut of its first series, or a counter that counts to its first value in that cell's spelling.

InsertModel.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PresentationPoint3d.description: A point in the 3D space, in canvas units: x right from the slide's left edge, y up from its bottom edge, z toward the viewer.

PresentationRotation3d.description: How a 3D object turns, in degrees about the 3D space's axes (x right, y up, z toward the viewer), in Cinema 4D's HPB order: heading about y, then pitch about its own x, then bank about its own z, three.js's YXZ Euler. A positive z turns it counterclockwise on the slide, a positive x tilts its top toward the viewer and a positive y brings its left side forward. With the rotation mode "quaternion" it is a quaternion instead, `w` and `x`, `y`, `z` in the same axes, which a key interpolates part by part and the turn reads normalized. A model's Blender quaternion (w, x, y, z), exported to glTF with +Y up, is (w, x, z, −y) here.

PresentationRotationMode.description: The rotation mode, of the two of Blender's the format takes: absent, Euler degrees; `quaternion`, a quaternion (WXYZ).

PresentationScale3d.description: A 3D object's scale along its own x, y and z axes.

ConstraintSource.description: A model's constraint as the file spells it.

AimSource.description: An Aim as the file spells it, each key but its id, type and target left out where it is Blender's default.

mode.description: How the volume is kept: whatever scale the other axes hold, while the model scales evenly, or while only the free axis scales.

free-axis.description: The axis that scales as keyed; the other two follow.

SquashAndStretchSource.description: A Squash and Stretch as the file spells it, each key but its id and type left out where it is Blender's default.

InsertLight.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PresentationAreaShape.description: An area light's shape, as Redshift's Area Shape names its two: a rectangle, or a disk, round or oval.

InsertShadowCatcher.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PresentationCatcherOrientation.description: The axis a shadow catcher's face looks along at no turn: y lying flat, z standing as a wall.

InsertFloor.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PresentationFloorPosition.description: Where a floor stands: its height above the slide's bottom edge, in canvas units.

anyOf.description: The stroke's color, or a gradient spanning the frame that paints it, as Figma's gradient stroke.

InsertPathD.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

anyOf.description: The stroke's color, or a gradient spanning the frame that paints it, as Figma's gradient stroke.

InsertPathPoints.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PathThroughPoint.description: A point a curve passes through; a corner keeps a sharp angle there instead of a smooth turn.

ObjectPropertyChangeSource.description: One property and its value in the file's words; null restores its default.

ObjectPropertySourceKey.description: A property's key in the file.

AgentObjectTransformSource.description: A transform as the file names a line's ends.

AgentSpaceTransform.description: A 3D object's move: any parts of its position, its whole rotation in its rotation mode and any parts of a model's or a light's scale. The parts it leaves out stay as they are.

AgentTransformFrame.description: The frame a transform gives an object: every side, but a table's height only where the edit sizes the table. A text box that grows to its words may leave its height out, as a height sizes nothing there.

PresentationPasteObjectSource.description: A pasted object, in the file's words.

anyOf.description: The letters' color, or a gradient spanning the text's box that paints them, as Keynote's Gradient Fill.

PasteText.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PasteTable.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PasteImage.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PasteAudio.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PasteShape.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

anyOf.description: The stroke's color, or a gradient spanning the frame that paints it, as Figma's gradient stroke.

PastePath.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PasteIcon.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PasteLine.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PresentationPastedConnectorAnchor.description: A pasted line end on an object of the same paste, by index as `parentIndex`; `at` is where it stands until attached.

PasteGroup.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PasteComposition.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

anyOf.description: The letters' color, or a gradient spanning the text's box that paints them, as Keynote's Gradient Fill.

PasteChart.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PasteModel.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PasteLight.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PasteShadowCatcher.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

PasteFloor.description: One object's keys and values as the file spells them.

name.description: The theme's name for create and rename; the layout's name for saveSlide.

theme.description: A theme's key or name from themes.list.

from.description: The theme key or name the layout is in.

layout.description: The layout's key in from, as themes.list gives it.

to.description: The theme key or name it goes to.

destination.description: Absolute path of a new .mptheme file outside any presentation folder; the result names it in files.

AgentThemeManageRequest.description: The theme chooser's own commands, and Save slide as layout. A new theme starts as a copy of the one in use; a layout is copied or moved into another theme by its key from `themes.list`; export writes a .mptheme file and install adds one, from paths where the app would ask with a dialog.

theme.description: The theme created, renamed, installed or given the layout; the one exported. By its key and name.

layout.description: The layout's key in the theme it was copied, moved or saved to, which setSlideLayout and insertSlide take.

AgentSlidesResizeRequest.description: Slide size, as the Presentation panel changes it: the theme and the slides scale together. A change of aspect needs rescale: fit keeps everything on the slide, fill covers it.

AgentSlideDimension.description: A slide's width or height in canvas units, as the .mdpoint file holds it.; canvas units

status.description: noChange when the slides already have the size.

rescaled.description: The policy the slides were rescaled by; null when nothing changed.

themeRevision.description: Needed when the step is a theme edit: `themeRevision` from `themes.get` or `themes.edit`.

AgentHistoryRequest.description: Edit > Undo or Redo: the presentation's one history, slide and theme steps alike. It moves only while nothing changed since the revisions given, so an agent undoing its own change never undoes someone else's later edit.

status.description: noChange when there was no step to take.

slideId.description: The id of a slide that isn't skipped to start at, as presentations.get lists it; omit for the first such slide.

confirmWebVideoNotice.description: Set true only when repeating a start that was refused with a web-video notice, after accepting its limitations; the agent path never opens its native warning dialog.

time.description: Seconds in the current step, derived from the session clock; Start is zero.

dropped.description: Frames that came late: intervals over one and a half of the display's usual interval.

AgentFrameProbe.description: How the audience window painted its last continuous playback, from each frame's own timestamp.

slideId.description: The slide to enter at Start, by its id as the show captured it.

AgentEnterEffect.description: The Animate tab's builds, as core names them.

SlideSize.description: A slide's size in canvas units.

min.description: Number inputs: the range a binding maps from; both or neither.

options.description: Choice inputs: the admitted values, the default among them.

PresentationPropertyChangeSource.description: One of the presentation's own properties and its value, as the file keys and spells it; null takes it away.

anyOf.description: Complete semantic value, or null to omit the property; null scheme returns to the layout's.

SlidePropertyChangeSource.description: One of a slide's own properties and its value, as the file keys and spells it.

ChoiceRenames.description: Options of choices renamed in place, by control: each old option's words to its new words.

ControlRenames.description: Controls renamed: each old name to its new name.

duration.description: Minimum seconds for this section; left out or 0, it lasts as long as what it holds.

start.description: Plays without a click of its own: with the step before it, or after that step ends, as PowerPoint's With Previous and After Previous do. Its times then count from that start. On the first step it plays after the transition. Omitted, the step waits for a click.

repeat.description: Play the section this many times before it completes; omitted plays once.

PresentationStepInputSource.description: A step as a proposal spells it; its curves may be left out, as a step that only waits or cues has none.

exponential-scale.description: On a `scale` or `crop.scale` change: reach `to` at one rate of zoom, as a camera push does; absent, it changes evenly.

AgentTweenChangeSource.description: A tween's change in the file's words.

anyOf.description: The Animate tab's and the timeline's timing edits, each as the app makes it.

AgentStepEditSource.description: A timing edit in the file's words: `loop-from` and a key's `exponential-scale`, and a swing's `wave-shape`.

PresentationCommentMutation.description: Each comment command is one standalone, undoable operation.

before.description: The words as read; a text changed since refuses the replacement.

PresentationTextReplacementTarget.description: Null objectId addresses the slide's speaker notes.

block.description: Its place among the text's nonempty blocks, from 0; a cue names a paragraph by id.

id.description: A lowercase UUID, as every id the contract mints.

anyOf.description: The operations as the kernel spells them, in the model's words (`strokeColor`, a fill as `{ kind, color }`): what the app runs once it has read an operation's file words.
Initial text and file values keyed by inherited object id.
Makes the slide a composition, a reusable scene other slides place; `size`, `controls` and `name` belong to it alone.
A composition's own size; only with `role: composition`.
A composition's controls; only with `role: composition`.
A composition's name; only with `role: composition`.
Minted when omitted; the batch may place slides against it, and later proposals change its objects.

afterStepId.description: Insert after this step; null means first, omitted means last.

stepIds.description: The new steps' ids, one per step, so a later `updateStep` or `tween` of the same batch, or the next proposal, keys them without reading them back; minted when omitted.

loop-from.description: Step seconds where the loop while waiting begins; null removes the loop.

start.description: When the move into this key begins, in section seconds; until then the value before it holds. Absent, at the key before.

time.description: Nonnegative seconds, kept to the microsecond.

interpolation.description: Interpolation into this key, from the preceding key or section start.

path.description: On a path pair's x key, `frame.x` or `translation.x`: the move into it, with the pair's y key there, bends along this path.

value.description: Null clears an optional property; its current type-style/default then applies.
Original interpolation endpoint, admitted against the same target as value.

end.description: Original endpoint in section seconds; must be at or after time and does not extend the section.

incoming.description: Preserve an interpolation prefix before this key; at time, value applies immediately.

exponential-scale.description: Whether the move to this key scales at an even rate, as After Effects' Exponential Scale does.

oscillate.description: A swing added from this key on, its wave named as the file names it.

keys.description: Shared key/cue ID namespace. An existing ID replaces the whole event; outer null deletes it.

time.description: Nonnegative seconds, kept to the microsecond.

loops.description: Each named curve's loop whole, its word and the keyframe it loops from; null takes it off. No key's edit changes it.

start.description: Play with the step before it or after it ends, within its click; null waits for a click.

repeat.description: Play the step this many times; null plays once.

AgentPresentationOperation.description: Operations the app serves as a kernel batch or one standalone step, in the words the .mdpoint file spells objects and properties in (`stroke`, `fill: accent`, `crop.focal-point`). The kernel owns semantics; closed-shape validation runs before it sees them. An object edit with `at` lands in the slide's motion as the Inspector's does with the playhead there: keys at that time, or Start values.

code.description: `no-change` when the proposal leaves the presentation as it is, so an idempotent caller tells it from a refusal.

operation.description: Index into the proposal's operations when the issue belongs to one.

revision.description: The presentation's revision with the change in it.

ids.description: The sections, comments, slides, objects and steps the change created or deleted.

skipped.description: Objects the change left as they were because they are locked.

root.description: Absolute presentation root; omitted means the focused presentation, or the only open one when no window is focused.

revision.description: On stale-revision: the revision the presentation is at now.

validation.description: On validation-failed from proposals.create or proposals.accept: everything the proposal's validation found.

AgentErrorCode.description: What went wrong. `unavailable` and `timeout` are also the front doors' own: the CLI and MCP give them when the app can't be reached or doesn't answer in time. The guide's code table says what each means and what to do.
